# 1.2.80 - tunnels and stairs, Find Passage, Frisk, and one dice look for the table

Stage E80 in full, both parts: tunnels and stairs between rooms, Find Passage, Foundry's secret doors, and Frisk, the Palm tile's
third direction. Stage E16 in part: its first part, Daggerheart's roll window before its context and one Dice So Nice look for the
table. E16's second part (the actions' thresholds, one card each, one Class Trial filter for Analyze) is not in this version. None
of it has been tried at a real table yet (Known gaps).

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **One dice look for the table.** The new world setting **One dice look for the table** is on by default and is a full
   Gamemaster's to change; it asks for a reload. On, every player and Assistant GM throws Dice So Nice dice and effects in the
   look of one full Gamemaster, fixed the first time the game runs with it on, and a change of their own goes back to it. A full
   Gamemaster's own look stays theirs, and each person keeps their own display and performance settings. Which full
   Gamemaster: while none is named, the primary GM's own user if that is a full Gamemaster, else the full Gamemaster with the
   lowest id; the primary GM then records the name. A player who picks a look for themselves or on their character
   reads "Your dice look is set by the GM." once a session. Turning the setting off writes nothing and gives nobody their old look
   back. An Assistant GM is held to it like a player; its change of the setting, or of
   whose look it is, is put back, and the primary GM reads "{name} changed the table's dice look settings, which only a full
   Gamemaster may change, so they were put back." A look that keeps changing straight back is left as it is for a minute, and the
   GM reads "{name}'s dice look keeps changing straight back, so it is left as it is for a minute, then put back at its next
   change or throw." once a session.
3. **Frisk's switch.** The new world setting **Frisk: forcing after a refusal** is on by default and is a GM's to change, with no
   reload. Off, an open Frisk only asks: a refusal or no answer ends it.
4. **A Frisk, a Take and a Plant at a body the GMs keep read as at a living student, by the owner's choice.** A student whose
   death the GMs keep secret is still alive for the table; the owner chose on 20.10 that a Frisk, a Take or a Plant at such a body
   is not told apart from one at a living student. An unseen Frisk there is noticed or not by its dice and read to the searcher as
   at a living student, and a Take or a Plant reads to the thief as at a living victim; the design had such a Frisk always
   unnoticed. The body's own card goes to the GMs alone, with no sound. A Take or a Plant at such a body really moves the item off
   or onto the body, as at a living victim, and has no Undo; the GMs read the thief's card and, when the thief was noticed, the
   body's. The card a living victim of a Palm Take or Plant reads is now shown in nobody's voice in the chat too (veiled), as a
   Frisk's card is.
5. **A Frisk's interrupted card is two sentences.** The card that ends a Frisk whose moment has passed reads "The moment has
   passed: this cannot be done now.", and "Your action is back." is said only by the browser that hands a paid action back. A
   searcher whose page reloaded or disconnected while its ask was open keeps the action spent when the ask ends this way, and its
   card does not say otherwise. The design had one card with both sentences.
6. **Foundry's secret doors are put back.** While a GM is connected, the primary GM's browser puts a Foundry secret door that a
   player opened or closed back as a GM last left it. A door no GM has changed is taken as it stands, and an open one stays open.
   A door changed while no GM was connected is put back when a GM connects, and the GM reads "{n} secret doors changed with no GM
   watching were put back as a GM last left them: {scenes}." (one door reads in the singular). A step through such a door is
   judged as a step through a wall.
7. **The move check keeps its default.** Under **Note it in the Debug log**, a player's token moved through a wall, a jump to a
   tunnel's far end or to another floor included, is noted and not undone: the character counts where the token stands, and the
   log row tells the GM. With **Send the token back**, a move to another floor where no stairs lead is sent back, and the GMs read
   "{name}'s token was moved to another floor on {scene} where no stairs lead, and was sent back where it stood."
8. **Give every room an ordinary entrance, still.** Every player sees a token leave one end of a tunnel and stand by the other, as
   they see any token move, and a room that only a tunnel or a passage reaches gives it away.
9. **Settings, keys and texts.** Five new settings (140 registered, 135 at 1.2.79): the two world switches above and three hidden
   ones, `diceLookSource` (the full Gamemaster whose look is the table's) and `diceLookWorld` (a world copy of the GMs' record of
   each character's dice look) in the world, and `gmDiceLooks` (the GMs' copy of each character's dice look) per browser. No new
   keybinding (3, as at 1.2.79). `lang/en.json` goes from 3545 to 3693 strings (148 added, none removed, 7 reworded),
   `lang/pl.json` from 4322 to 4488 (166 added, none removed, 11 reworded). Reworded: the opening rolls' titles lose "your roll"
   ("Opening the murder", "Something feels wrong", "Going through with it"), a locked roll window's tooltip reads "Who sees this
   roll is set by the game, not here.", the Take row's hint reads "Lift one thing out of their pockets. What comes out is whatever
   comes out - a critical lets you choose.", and an open passage says "Open" in the State column where it said "Secret"; and the Passages tab's
   footnote gains a line on Make public and Make secret. Texts a GM acts on: the dice look cards above, the secret doors card above, and, when a Frisk is asked of a body the GMs keep, "{who}
   asks {target} to turn out their pockets. {target} is a body you keep, so nobody is asked: in {s} seconds {who} hears that there
   is no answer. You may open the discovery yourself."

## At the table

### Tunnels and stairs, for the GM

- Room Setup's **Passages** tab has **+ Tunnel or stairs**: a click in each of two rooms, on one floor or two.
- The tab says "Click the square where the tunnel begins, inside a room. For stairs, switch to the other floor before the second
  click. Esc cancels."
- A click in no room, both ends in one room, or an end on a square where another tunnel already ends is refused with the reason,
  for example "Another tunnel already ends on that square."
- The tab's columns are now Rooms, Kind, Shape, Origin, Who knows, At season start and State.
- Kind says Public or Secret, Shape says In a wall or Tunnel or stairs, and Origin says GM or Secret door.
- A passage a student found with Find Passage is listed as found.
- **Close** takes a tunnel's marks and ends off the knowers' screens with the way.
- On a knower's screen a tunnel's end is marked with the room it leads to, named once they have found that room, and a room they
  have not found is numbered.
- **Make public**, beside Close, gives a passage to every student at once and tells nobody: no card, no sound.
- It lifts no lock, and the season's reset keeps it public.
- **Make secret** gives the passage back to the students listed in its row alone; a show made while it was public is not kept.
- Revoking a student from a public passage closes nothing at once: it decides whether they still know it after Make secret.

### For a student who knows a tunnel

- A student at one of a tunnel's ends presses **Go through** beside the tunnel under **Known passages** on their sheet.
- "At one of its ends" means within one square of it, a distance that was chosen and not measured.
- The primary GM's browser decides it as it decides a door: one crossing at a door's price, or one Eclipse crossing during an
  Eclipse.
- Somebody else's bedroom is passed, and the Mastermind passes a locked door and a sealed room this way too.
- A locked door, a sealed room, being Chained, a running incident, a Class Trial, a price the student cannot pay and a spent
  Eclipse turn them back in a door's words, and nothing is paid.
- The token lands on the far end's square, or the nearest free square of that end's room, on that end's floor; if the token cannot
  be moved there, the price is given back.
- It needs a GM connected, and every player sees the token leave one end and stand by the other.

### Find Passage

- **Find Passage** is Analyze's fourth choice: Head against 16, 1 action, offered in every room and refused in a Class Trial
  before anything is paid.
- The row reads "Go over the walls of this room for a way through that nobody shows. {n}+ opens one secret passage here to you."
  and the roll window "Finding a secret passage: {n}+."
- 16 or a critical finds the oldest open secret passage of the student's room on their floor that they do not know, a stretch of
  its wall or a tunnel's end, and they know it from then on; the Mastermind finds none, knowing them all.
- Whatever comes of it, the student and the GMs get one card of the same shape - a find, or "You find no hidden passage here." for
  a miss, an empty room and the Mastermind - and an onlooker reads nothing.
- A find reads "There is a secret passage in this room, to {to}. Where the way is open, your map shows it."
- A trap can be set to trigger on a Find Passage: the trigger reads "Somebody hunts for a secret passage here".
- A Reroll that beats 16 finds once, in the room its roll was thrown in and only while the student still stands there; one that
  falls below takes back only what its own roll found.
- A Reroll of a Find Stash that beats 16 opens one stash, and one that falls below leaves a stash it opened open.
- The season's reset takes what was found and keeps the tunnels.
- A secret passage opening to a student has its own sound, in the World category.

### Foundry's secret doors and the players' rulers

- The map check names each Foundry secret door with "A Foundry secret door".
- Season setup has the row "No Foundry secret doors (recommended)" with **Convert to passages**: "Any player can open a Foundry
  secret door, and their character walks through it. Convert to passages makes each one an ordinary wall, shut; where it stands
  between two rooms it is also a secret passage nobody knows yet - give it to a student in the Passages tab. One that stands
  between no two rooms is a plain wall."
- The row beside it, "The players' movement ruler is hidden (optional)", has **Hide** and **Show**: "While a player drags a token,
  the whole table sees the route it takes - through a secret passage too. Hide takes the ruler from the Player and Trusted Player
  roles, and Show gives it back. The GM roles keep theirs."

### Frisk, the Palm tile's third direction

- The Palm window has a third row, **Frisk: see what they carry**: "Look through their pockets and take nothing."
- It aims at a student in the room, costs 1 action, moves nothing and writes no item, no flag on a character and no setting.
- **Openly** is the default choice: "Ask them to turn out their pockets. If they refuse or do not answer, you can make them: Body
  {force}+, in front of the room." Body is 12 and the force window is 30 seconds.
- The target's player is asked "Turn out your pockets?" with "Let them look" and "Refuse", and no answer in a minute counts as a
  refusal.
- The GMs answer for a character without a player; if the player is away, nobody is asked and the searcher hears at once that
  there is no answer, and may force it.
- After a refusal or no answer the searcher is asked "Make them?" with "Make them" and "Leave it": "Body {force}+. The whole room
  will see it. You have {s} seconds to decide."
- A force that wins shows the searcher the list; one that fails leaves the target reading "{who} tries to force you to turn out
  your pockets. You shake them off." The whole room reads what happened, and a Monocub in the room is among the witnesses.
- An allow shows the pockets as they were at the ask: "This is what they had on them when you asked."
- **Unseen** is two rolls on one payment: Shadow 15 so they do not notice, then Hand 10 to get a proper look.
- The list goes to the searcher and the GMs alone; after an Unseen Frisk the target is told only when it noticed.
- What the searcher reads: "{who} is carrying:" "{who} has nothing in their pockets." "You do not get a proper look at what {who}
  is carrying."
- The list never shows a Truth Bullet or a stash, an item no GM has decided on is left out, and a trapped item reads as its
  untrapped twin.
- A body the frisker knows is not frisked ("That is a body now. Look through it from its sheet. Your action is back."), and a
  Frisk is refused outside a room both students stand in, in an Eclipse, in a Class Trial and in the asker's own incident.
- A Frisk on a body the GMs keep, or on somebody in the incident, asks nobody and plays as a student who does not answer; the GMs
  get a notice and may open the discovery by hand.
- With no GM connected the Frisk is refused before it is paid: "An action roll waits for a GM: no GM is connected, so the action
  was not taken and nothing was paid."
- A Reroll keeps the moment: a miss nobody felt can still turn into one look. A force stands, with "The dice are rewritten, but
  the moment is not. The whole room saw how it went.", and so does a Frisk the target felt, with "The dice are rewritten, but the
  moment is not. They already know whether you got a proper look."
- Foundry sends every browser a character's items, so an item's name in a Frisk's list is a known limit.

### The roll window and one dice look

- With **Lock the roll window for players** on, a player's roll window shows one summary line that says what the roll is, with "no
  modifiers" where it has none, and Roll; the locked sections are hidden.
- A Call that opens the experiences or the trait leaves their section; a GM's window stays whole.
- The mode select is a chip that says who sees the roll: "The GMs and you" while rolls are forced private, "The GMs, you and the
  room" for a Monocub, and otherwise the select's own mode, "Public" for a public one.
- The opening and crisis throws keep their Reaction chip on action, with "This roll's Hope or Despair decides what happens next,
  so it is an action, never a reaction." in the tooltip.
- The window is set to open below the curtain's edge, not over the glass at the top of the screen, and a long title is kept from
  widening it; this is read in the stylesheet and in the tests' stand-in window, not seen (LIVE-E16-02).
- A player at 0 Hope who bought an Experience Call can click the experience and Roll stays on, at no cost.
- A Meddle's -1 is on the roll window before it is drawn, the lock on or off.
- Where Daggerheart's roll window is not of the shape the module reads, the console says so once and the window works as before.
- A Find Passage or a Frisk thrown through the roll window keeps its context.
- The primary GM writes the look of the full Gamemaster that is the table's source onto every user below a full Gamemaster and
  puts a change back; how a throw is then drawn in Dice So Nice is not seen (LIVE-E16-03).

### The handbooks

- GM: section 1 (the settings paragraph, the dice look), 2 (the two Season setup rows), 5 (Analyze's Find Passage, Palm's Frisk),
  9.1 (the Passages tab's columns and buttons), 9.6 (tunnels, Go through, Make public, Find Passage, Foundry's secret doors, the
  rulers), 10 (Frisk) and 17 (the secret passage sound).
- Player: chapter 1 (Body's line, the roll window and the dice look), 3 (Secret passages), 4 (Analyze, Palm), 5 (Reroll) and 10
  (the opening roll's window) and the Student Brochure's Analyze and Palm lines.
- Each in English and Polish.

## Changed

- **New file**: `scripts/frisk.mjs` (the Frisk's ask, answer and force and its list, judged on the primary GM); 149 files
  in `scripts/`, 148 at 1.2.79.
- **Tunnels and Find Passage** are in `passages.mjs`, `passages-gm.mjs`, `passages-tab.mjs`, `movement.mjs`, `sheet.mjs` and
  `gm-bridge.mjs`: the primary GM carries out Go through and judges Find Passage; `utils.mjs` gains `serialWrite`, which keeps one
  key's steps in order.
- **The dice look** moves into `dice-sync.mjs` (the primary GM puts back the two Dice So Nice flags on every user below a full
  Gamemaster and the overlays on characters) and the old road that sent Dice So Nice's client setting over the module's socket is
  gone; `roll-dialog.mjs` wraps `D20RollDialog.prototype._prepareContext`, with one new row in `patches.mjs`.
- **Tests**: 38 new numbered tests, R593-R623 (4 in tier 0, 27 in tier 1) and R800-R806 (5 in tier 0, 2 in tier 1); next free
  R807.
- There are 60 more tier-2 tests, which carry no number (952 titles in `scripts/tests-tier2.mjs`, 892 at 1.2.79).
- The scenario files are still 28, all in `ci`; scenarios 01, 15, 17, 30, 33, 40, 65, 72, 76 and 83 gain checks.
- `known-leaks.json` gains three entries, `foundry-actor-items`, `foundry-passage-tunnel` and `foundry-secret-door-type`, each
  with a marker in the README's Privacy paragraph (9 known leaks, 6 at 1.2.79).
- **The manifest's compatibility is unchanged**: Daggerheart `minimum` and `verified` 2.6.5, Foundry `minimum` 14.364 and
  `verified` 14.365.
- Outside the module: the CI workflow, the registry and stage tools and the repository's working notes changed too.
- The suite's files, `tools/check.mjs`, `tools/registry.mjs` and `tools/stages.mjs` read the text they match with Windows line
  ends (CRLF) as with LF line ends (105ea31), and `node tools/check.mjs contract` names a read in the suite's files that leaves that
  step out. Of `scripts/`, only the test files changed for it (`tests-kit.mjs`, `tests-lint.mjs` and the three tier files).
  The tier-2 test of a drawn roll refused for want of the GMs' marks now reads the reason of the refusal on the GM's console,
  and in the session log while the log, which keeps its first 60 rows, has room.

## Known gaps

- Nothing here has run on a real Foundry v14. Each of these is a live check not tried yet: a tunnel and stairs on a real canvas
  with a second player in both rooms, the token's move (teleport, displace, no animation, the floor write), the marks' look and
  the pick's floor switch (LIVE-E80-01); the players' movement ruler, with which roles Foundry 14 gives it by default, the module
  assuming Player and up (LIVE-E80-02); a player's change of a Foundry secret door on 14, with the GM's put-back, its notice and
  its stamps (LIVE-E80-03); the Passages tab in a real Room Setup window at 1366x768 and 1920x1080, in both themes, in English and
  Polish (LIVE-E80-04).
- Frisk on The Forge with two accounts: whether 5 seconds of grace is enough for an answer or a **Make them** pressed in the last
  second, whether 10 seconds is enough for a force's roll, the minute of silence in real time, a GM who drops and comes back
  without a reload, and a new primary GM whose clock runs ahead (LIVE-E80-05).
- The owner's own run of Frisk on the sandbox (three accounts, a witness, an offline player, an NPC, a body the GMs keep, an
  incident and the Mastermind as target, in English and Polish, in both themes) has no live id and has not been done.
- The roll window and the dice look: Roll greyed from the costs on Daggerheart 2.10.5 and on the table's version, and S02-04 on it
  (LIVE-E16-01); every action window in both themes at 1366x768, with the window clearing a sheet's tabs below the curtain, the
  title bar, and a long title (LIVE-E16-02); a player's throw in Dice So Nice looking like the GM's, with how Dice So Nice builds
  a look from a colour and what it does with an unlinked token's actor (LIVE-E16-03); on Foundry 14, an Assistant primary's write
  of another user's account, a write that fires no hook, who the world setting names as its last writer, and the race of a
  put-back on a real server (LIVE-E16-04).
- Part of E16-14, every action window in both themes, waits for E16's second part.
- **Frisk's windows.** The Palm window with Frisk picked still scrolls at 1366x768 (86 px under Stained Glass, 82 px in English
  and 69 px in Polish under Monokuma Legacy) and "Whose pockets?" lies below the fold, with its buttons in view; this was drawn in
  Chromium in a stand-in frame with the module's stylesheets, not in Foundry's own window, and the pictures are not in the
  repository (P2-01, OPEN).
- A Frisk's windows were mocked up after their code, not before it as the plan wanted.
- Not measured: a second GM (the checks add one to the list of users and never connect one), a reload of the primary GM in the
  middle of an ask, a GM leaving, two owners answering apart, an answer that comes after the searcher's wait, the target leaving
  between the two draws, a GM's own Frisk's Reroll and a death at the Reroll.
- An Eclipse or a Class Trial that starts in the middle of an ask is read at the next answer, follow or clock, not at once.
- A follow sent while no GM is connected gets no answer and hands nothing back; if the primary GM ends an ask and then reloads
  before the follow comes, the follow reads as interrupted and hands back an action the end left spent (read in the code, not
  measured).
- A GM who drops and comes back without a reload is read by another GM's force as one that forgot its asks: no dice, "The moment
  has passed: this cannot be done now.", the ask is let go and the action stays spent, though that GM still held it (read in the
  code, not measured).
- An ask the primary GM drops while another GM's roll window is open hands the action back, but the dice were thrown and the
  window's Calls stay spent; the same holds for a GM's own force whose gate shuts in its roll window, which counts for nothing.
- A target who becomes a body the GMs keep while an open Frisk's ask is running ends the ask as interrupted, where a living
  target's ask goes on; this is a rules decision that was not made.
- The same class outside Frisk is unchanged: giving an item to a recipient the GMs keep dead tells the giver "That cannot be done
  now." where a living recipient takes it, and a Monocub's Meddle at such a body is refused with "Confusion does not reach them.
  The moment passed before it landed." after the Monocub's browser has paid.
- The absence of a sound at a body is read in the code and not heard.
- The handbooks' Frisk sentences are read off the code, not played at a table, and the Polish GM handbook's new Palm sentence
  writes 'GM-a', a form 17 older lines also use, where the book mostly writes 'GMa' (131 times).
- **Tunnels and passages.** Go through is not measured with a second GM, a GM on another scene, no GM, a reload or a Monocub; the
  reach of one square and the landing's three rings are chosen.
- The Analyze window's Find Passage row and the two sounds heard, the Reroll's lines and the stash card a replay posts are not
  measured at a table.
- A Find Stash's first throw still searches the room the token document names, not the room the GMs read; a Reroll's stash replay
  springs no stash-hunt trap; a GM's own Find Stash Reroll is run by no test.
- The crossing, action and rest traps are still raised on the acting player's browser and relayed, and not yet on the GM that
  judges them.
- A secret door with no record that a player changes while no GM is connected, before any pass has recorded it, is taken as it
  stands by the next pass.
- A player made a GM who then becomes the primary runs no secret-door pass until that browser's next start.
- A GM leaving while a put-back has not landed is measured on plain objects, and an actor's type change on Foundry 14 on plain
  objects, not on a real actor; the Passages tab's floor switch is measured on a fake scene.
- A converted wall's door sound and animation are read from Foundry 14's schema and not written on a real one; a white ring's tint
  and a text colour under Stained Glass are not seen on a real canvas.
- The console API `game.drpg.passages` has no make-public or make-secret call, the GMs' overlay draws a public passage like a
  secret one, and the list of students a public passage was not delivered to names every student whose player was not sent the
  copy.
- What a reader understands of the new handbook text is not measured.
- **The dice look.** A character that an Assistant GM makes with a dice look of its own while no full Gamemaster is connected has
  no record, and the next full Gamemaster's load takes its look as found where no player owns the character (one a player owns
  is taken with none); the owner has not decided the rule.
- A full Gamemaster's look on an unlinked token is put back at the first throw a user below full Gamemaster makes as it.
- An Assistant primary judges against its own browser's copy until a full Gamemaster loads, and takes no world copy an Assistant
  wrote last.
- Three questions of E16 run on their defaults and wait for the owner (Q5: an Assistant GM may not switch the setting or choose
  whose look it is; Q6: a world copy of the GMs' dice looks that only a full Gamemaster writes; Q7: the opening rolls' shorter
  titles).
- Known leaks whose stages have not shipped, unchanged: a secret project's name in Daggerheart's countdowns (until E43), an
  unfound trace's hidden token (until E60), and a character killed in secret heard in the main room on the voice tile (until E19).
  New Foundry limits: a token seen going through a tunnel, Foundry's secret doors seen on every map, and every item a character
  carries.
